newsitem.title: PERU: Cementos Lima aims to export in region in 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Cementos Lima aims to export in region in 4 years.

text.p: Peru's largest cement firm, Cementos Lima, aims to begin exporting clinker and cement to other countries in the region before the end of the century thanks to a $185 million expansion program intended to more than double production capacity.

"Our aim is to get our products out to neigboring markets that have a high level of construction and whose cement companies do not cover all the demand," the company's manager, Carlos Ugas, told Reuters.

He added Cementos Lima was 70 percent through this year's $135 million part of the expansion plan, which should raise production capacity at its only plant to an annual level of 2.3 million tonnes of clinker and 2.5 million tonnes of cement.
This would compare to current annual production capacity of 1.15 million tonnes of clinker and 1.7 million tonnes of cement annually.

The second part of the expansion plan, which would cost $50 million and be completed by 1998, should raise production capacity further to 3.45 million tonnes of clinker and three million tonnes of cement, added company president Juan Aguirre Roca.
The officials said the decision to expand the plant was based on projections for a recovery in the construction sector, which contracted 6.4 percent in the first nine months, towards the end of 1996.
